content.value: Artificial Intelligence is the field focused on building systems that can perform tasks which typically require human intelligence, such as reasoning, pattern recognition, and decision making.

concepts.name: Artificial intelligence
concepts.description: Computer systems designed to perform tasks that normally require human-like perception, reasoning, prediction, generation, or decision-making.

concepts.name: Intelligent agent
concepts.description: A system that observes an environment, reasons over what it observes, and takes actions toward a goal.

concepts.name: Perception
concepts.description: The process of turning sensory or input data into usable information about the world or task.

concepts.name: Reasoning
concepts.description: The process of drawing conclusions, making inferences, or choosing actions from available information.

concepts.name: Prediction
concepts.description: An estimated output about an unknown value, future event, label, or outcome.

concepts.name: Decision-making
concepts.description: Choosing an action or recommendation based on goals, constraints, evidence, or predicted outcomes.

content.value: Weak (or narrow) AI is designed to handle specific tasks, while strong AI would match or exceed human intelligence across many domains. Today, most real-world systems are examples of weak AI.

concepts.name: Narrow AI
concepts.description: AI designed to perform a specific task or limited family of tasks rather than general human-level reasoning.

concepts.name: General AI
concepts.description: A hypothetical AI system with broad, flexible intelligence across many domains and tasks.

concepts.name: Strong AI
concepts.description: The idea of AI that would genuinely understand, reason, and possess mind-like intelligence rather than only simulate task performance.

concepts.name: Weak AI
concepts.description: AI that performs intelligent-looking tasks without requiring human-like understanding or consciousness.

concepts.name: Task-specific intelligence
concepts.description: Capability that works well inside a defined task boundary but may not transfer to unrelated problems.

concepts.name: Capability boundary
concepts.description: The practical limit of where an AI system is expected to work reliably and where its behavior becomes uncertain.

questions.question: Which type of AI do current real-world systems like recommendation engines represent?

content.value: AI is used in recommendation systems, voice assistants, image recognition, fraud detection, and more. Many of these systems rely on pattern recognition over large datasets.

concepts.name: Recommendation system
concepts.description: A system that ranks or suggests items, content, or actions based on user behavior, item features, or learned patterns.

concepts.name: Computer vision
concepts.description: AI methods for interpreting visual inputs such as images, video, objects, scenes, and spatial patterns.

concepts.name: Natural language processing
concepts.description: AI methods for analyzing, generating, transforming, or extracting meaning from human language.

concepts.name: Speech recognition
concepts.description: The task of converting spoken audio into text or structured language representations.

concepts.name: Autonomous system
concepts.description: A system that senses, decides, and acts with limited or no direct human control in its operating environment.

concepts.name: Decision support
concepts.description: Software that helps people evaluate options, risks, recommendations, or likely outcomes before making a decision.

content.value: AI systems can be brittle, biased, and dependent on the data they are trained on. They do not possess human judgment, common sense, or real understanding.

concepts.name: Brittleness
concepts.description: A failure mode where a system performs well in expected cases but breaks under small changes, edge cases, or unfamiliar inputs.

concepts.name: Bias
concepts.description: A systematic pattern in data or model behavior that produces distorted, unfair, or unrepresentative outcomes.

concepts.name: Data dependence
concepts.description: The way an AI system’s behavior is constrained by the quality, coverage, and assumptions of the data used to build it.

concepts.name: Hallucination
concepts.description: A generated output that sounds plausible but is unsupported, fabricated, or incorrect.

concepts.name: Common-sense reasoning
concepts.description: Everyday background reasoning about the world that humans often use implicitly but AI systems may lack.

concepts.name: Accountability
concepts.description: Clear responsibility for how a system is designed, deployed, monitored, and corrected when it causes problems.

content.value: Machine Learning is a subset of AI where systems learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed with rules.

concepts.name: Machine learning
concepts.description: A branch of AI where systems learn patterns from data instead of being programmed with every rule explicitly.

concepts.name: Training data
concepts.description: Examples used to fit a model’s parameters or decision patterns during learning.

concepts.name: Model
concepts.description: A learned mathematical or computational representation used to make predictions, classifications, generations, or decisions.

concepts.name: Feature
concepts.description: An input variable or measurable signal used by a model to learn or make predictions.

concepts.name: Label
concepts.description: Text associated with a form control to identify what input is expected.

concepts.name: Prediction
concepts.description: An estimated output about an unknown value, future event, label, or outcome.

content.value: In supervised learning, models are trained on labeled data. In unsupervised learning, models try to discover structure in unlabeled data, such as clusters or patterns.

concepts.name: Supervised learning
concepts.description: Learning from examples that include known target labels or values.

concepts.name: Unsupervised learning
concepts.description: Learning patterns, groups, or structure from data without labeled target answers.

concepts.name: Classification
concepts.description: A supervised learning task where the model assigns an input to one of several categories.

concepts.name: Regression
concepts.description: A supervised learning task where the model predicts a numeric value.

concepts.name: Clustering
concepts.description: An unsupervised learning task that groups similar examples together based on patterns in the data.

concepts.name: Dimensionality reduction
concepts.description: Techniques that represent data with fewer variables while preserving important structure or variation.

questions.question: Which learning type uses labeled examples like (image, label) pairs?

content.value: Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training data instead of learning general patterns. A well-generalized model performs well on new, unseen data.

concepts.name: Overfitting
concepts.description: When a model learns training examples too specifically and performs poorly on new data.

concepts.name: Generalization
concepts.description: A model’s ability to perform well on new examples that were not used during training.

concepts.name: Training set
concepts.description: The subset of data used to fit a model.

concepts.name: Test set
concepts.description: A held-out subset of data used to estimate how well a model performs on unseen examples.

concepts.name: Validation set
concepts.description: A held-out subset used during development to tune model choices without using the final test set.

concepts.name: Model complexity
concepts.description: The capacity of a model to represent patterns, often affecting both learning power and overfitting risk.

content.value: Spam detection is a classic ML application. Models learn from examples of 'spam' and 'not spam' emails, then classify new emails based on patterns they learned.

concepts.name: Problem framing
concepts.description: Defining the real-world task, inputs, outputs, success criteria, and constraints before building a model.

concepts.name: Input data
concepts.description: The data provided to a model or system for processing, prediction, or decision-making.

concepts.name: Target variable
concepts.description: The value or label a supervised model is trained to predict.

concepts.name: Model evaluation
concepts.description: The process of measuring whether a model performs well enough for its intended use.

concepts.name: Deployment context
concepts.description: The real environment where a model runs, including users, devices, latency, data availability, and operational constraints.

concepts.name: Prediction workflow
concepts.description: The sequence of steps that turns input data into a model output and routes that output to a user or system.
